concerns.text: Task T015 (scorer.py) is marked [P] (parallel-safe) but depends on the output of T013 (generator.py) and T014 (validator.py). The 'Dependencies & Execution Order' section correctly notes T013 must precede T015, yet the [P] tag implies it can run in parallel with other tasks without dependencies. This is a semantic violation: a task consuming generated artifacts cannot be parallel-safe relative to its producer.

Task T027 (wbench_suite.py) is marked [P] but depends on the video artifacts generated by T021/T023 (inference). The 'Dependencies' section states 'Inference (T021) must precede metrics calculation (T027)'. Marking T027 as [P] suggests it has no dependencies, which contradicts the data-flow requirement that it consumes inference outputs.

Task T028 (correlation.py) is marked [P] but depends on the metrics calculated in T027. The 'Dependencies' section explicitly states 'Metrics (T027) must precede correlation analysis (T028)'. The [P] tag is incorrect as this task cannot run until T027 produces the input data.

The test tasks (T009-T011) are marked [P] and placed before implementation tasks (T012-T017). While TDD is a valid strategy, the 'Dependencies' section states 'Tests (if included) MUST be written and FAIL before implementation'. However, T009/T010 depend on the *existence* of the code in T013/T015 to test. If T013/T015 don't exist, the tests cannot run (they would fail to import). The ordering implies tests run before code exists, which is a logical dependency violation unless the tests are strictly 'stub' tests. Clarify if these are import-tests or logic-tests.
